title: Embeddings/rerank: configurable redaction, telemetry gating, and retention policy
creator: Aisha Nayar
description:
Problem:
Customer teams and internal routing pipelines sometimes need embeddings and rerank telemetry for quality and performance debugging, but current logs can include user-provided PII. We lack fine-grained controls for: per-tenant redaction levels, telemetry gating (which events are emitted), retention windows, and privacy-preserving sampling.

Goal:
Provide a configurable privacy pipeline for embeddings and rerank endpoints that lets customers and platform operators:
- Choose a redaction level (none, token-level scrub, entity-redact, or deterministic-hash) per-organization or per-route.
- Gate telemetry emission by event type (inference_request, kv_cache_fetch, rerank_scores, embeddings_vector) and by risk-class.
- Set retention windows per tenant for short-term debug traces vs. long-term metrics.
- Emit structured audit events with a compact schema that excludes raw inputs unless explicitly allowed.
- Integrate with KMS-backed encryption and customer-managed sinks for sensitive audit delivery.

Scope and non-goals:
In scope: server-side redaction hooks in the embeddings and rerank handlers, new config objects in tenant settings, audit-event schema, retention enforcement service, and UI controls in Console to view/set defaults.
Out of scope: client-side SDK changes (separate follow-up), differential-privacy algorithms applied to vectors (research-led follow-up).

Success criteria:
- No raw user text is stored in platform logs for tenants who opt into "strict" redaction.
- Per-tenant retention windows are enforced with automated deletion jobs and verifiable deletion logs.
- Telemetry gating reduces audit event volume by >= 70% for high-volume test tenants without losing critical debugging signals.
- Console exposes a simple three-state privacy control and per-route override with audit trail entries.

Design overview:
1) Redaction pipeline: a middleware layer attached to the embeddings/rerank request path. It applies one of four modes: PASS_THROUGH, TOKEN_SCRUB (regex + safe tokenizer-based removal), ENTITY_REDACT (NER-based scrub for names/emails/phones), HASHED_PAYLOAD (deterministic HMAC of input with tenant key). Mode chosen by tenant config; system-owned telemetry uses PASS_THROUGH only when allowed by tenant.
2) Telemetry gating: classify events into risk buckets at emission time. Config allows toggling emission for buckets and setting sampling rates. High-risk events (raw input, rerank debug traces) default to disabled for new tenants.
3) Audit schema: compact JSON lines including: event_type, timestamp, tenant_id (hashed for internal-only storage), route, model_version, signal_summary (short tokenized checksum), redaction_mode, retention_until, and optional encrypted_payload reference. Raw_payload only included when explicit consent flag is set.
4) Retention enforcement: retention_until set at event creation; background expirer deletes events and writes deletion audit entries encrypted with KMS. Expires are per-tenant and per-event-type.
5) Customer-managed sinks: for tenants that require full telemetry, support streaming audit events to customer S3/GCS with server-side encryption and choices to exclude raw_payload.

Constraints and tradeoffs:
- NER-based scrubbing can have false negatives; provide conservative safe defaults and allow customers to opt into stronger scrubbing.
- Hashing inputs preserves determinism for debugging but still exposes fingerprinted content; document security implications.
- Sampling reduces debug fidelity; we will expose sample rate micro-metrics in Console to help teams understand coverage.

Operational considerations:
- Add SLOs for the redaction middleware to ensure <1ms median additional latency for short requests and <5ms p99 under normal load.
- Add unit and property tests for scrubbers with corpora of synthetic PII.
- Plan an opt-in beta with a few existing customers before defaulting to strict mode for all new orgs.

acceptance_criteria: Config portal in Console to set tenant redaction mode and telemetry gates
Server middleware applies configured redaction mode for embeddings & rerank endpoints
Events include retention_until and redaction_mode fields in audit schema
Automated deletion job removes expired events and writes deletion audit entries
End-to-end integration test demonstrating PASS_THROUGH blocked by default for new tenants
technical_notes: Redaction modes: PASS_THROUGH | TOKEN_SCRUB | ENTITY_REDACT | HASHED_PAYLOAD. TOKEN_SCRUB will use tokenizer-aware regex to avoid breaking UTF-8 tokens. ENTITY_REDACT uses our NER service with a conservative threshold; fallback to TOKEN_SCRUB on NER failure. HASHED_PAYLOAD uses HMAC-SHA256 with tenant-specific key stored in KMS. Audit events will never store plaintext inputs unless tenant config explicit_allow_raw_payload=true. Retention enforcement implemented with TTL index in vector-store and a separate durable audit-log table with encrypted blobs. Provide a migration path to reprocess existing logs into redaction modes via a backfill job.

2025-02-17: Security review checklist drafted; Luca to schedule consult with Compliance on implications of HASHED_PAYLOAD
